topic: Parts of a volcano and active/inactive volcanoes
key_concepts: Molten rock beneath Earth's surface is called magma and comes from the mantle.
Molten rock that reaches Earth's surface is called lava.
Tiny particles emitted during a volcanic eruption are called ash.
The main conduit is the largest tube through which magma travels toward the surface.
Lava can also flow out through smaller side tubes or vents.
A crater is the bowl-shaped opening at the top of a volcano.
Active volcanoes have records of eruption activity.
Inactive volcanoes have no recorded eruptions.
Philippine examples of active volcanoes include Pinatubo, Taal, Mayon, and Bulusan.
Philippine examples of inactive volcanoes include Lobo, Palay-palay, Arayat, and Binitacan
Eruption dates can be used to compare and classify volcanoes as active or inactive.
